items.title: Language layers for Mistral Small 3.1 and InternVL3
items.content:
{
  "discussion": {
    "author_login": "gakada",
    "created_at": "2025-04-27T23:17:30Z",
    "kind": "pull_request",
    "number": 25,
    "state": "CLOSED",
    "title": "Language layers for Mistral Small 3.1 and InternVL3",
    "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/25"
  },
  "objects": [
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "They are the same Mistral/Qwen2/Llama layers, so quantization and text inference is already possible.",
      "content_sha256": "9da35d6cc5b2ae85ee28bb48d0f6a12b05637c470c1921bdce12ba1305fb35d0",
      "created_at": "2025-04-27T23:17:30Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-27T23:17:30Z",
      "source_id": "PR_kwDOOU24Gs6UFeZt",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/25"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "I've been holding off a little on Mistral 3.1 because I want to work out a sane way to support component models. Quantizing this way would give you Mistral 3.1 quants all over HF that won't work with the (upcoming, soon\u2122 ) multimodal features. Patching in support this way when it's \"easy\" has become a real headache in ExLlamaV2, and I'm trying to be a little more deliberate about it this time around. I'm still not sure exactly how it should look, but I plan to start architecting the multimodal support next week and I'll have a clearer picture then.\r\n\r\nAs for dynamic RoPE, it generally can't work with the current cache implementation since keys are stored after applying embeddings, so the cached keys wouldn't stay valid for a growing context. TBH I never fully understood how it's meant to work in Transformers either, since the usual caching looks like:\r\n\r\n```py\r\n        query_states = self.q_proj(hidden_states).view(hidden_shape).transpose(1, 2)\r\n        key_states = self.k_proj(hidden_states).view(hidden_shape).transpose(1, 2)\r\n        value_states = self.v_proj(hidden_states).view(hidden_shape).transpose(1, 2)\r\n\r\n        cos, sin = position_embeddings\r\n        query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)\r\n\r\n        if past_key_value is not None:\r\n            # sin and cos are specific to RoPE models; cache_position needed for the static cache\r\n            cache_kwargs = {\"sin\": sin, \"cos\": cos, \"cache_position\": cache_position}\r\n            key_states, value_states = past_key_value.update(key_states, value_states, self.layer_idx, cache_kwargs)\r\n```\r\n\r\nThen `@dynamic_rope_update` recomputes embeddings every time a token is added, but the cached keys are never updated to the new frequencies (and technically can't be without running the entire context through the forward pass, on every token.) I can see it working if keys are cached prior to embedding and RoPE is done on-the-fly, but there's a performance penalty for that, too, and support for fusing it into the attention step is patchy with both flash-attn and FlashInfer (which I'm hoping to migrate to when it supports more head dimensions.) So I've kind of been deliberately ignoring dynamic RoPE until it starts making sense to me. (:",
      "content_sha256": "6549e4cdfd25d6d0f7a073aab27f7679ac53d01c6d05d825a961bb74de9632fc",
      "created_at": "2025-04-28T00:17:45Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-28T00:17:45Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6o5xwu",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/25#issuecomment-2833718318"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "They are basically `MistralForCausalLM` and `Qwen2ForCausalLM` quants, so should still work, maybe with fixed `config.json` and `*.safetensors` (no requantization). Though I can also just convert to `MistralForCausalLM` and `Qwen2ForCausalLM` first and quantize that, so I removed the hack :ok_hand:\r\n\r\nThe dynamic RoPE in InternVL3 only happens past 32K context, at which point those models aren't very good anyway, so it is probably fine to have it as default. But it should be there because it can be in `config.json`.",
      "content_sha256": "9ad7cfa4df4aa3739a2cfe3853b94526bcbc577caaa62d0edeb4cee5714be80c",
      "created_at": "2025-04-28T03:17:43Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-28T03:17:43Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6o6Y58",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/25#issuecomment-2833878652"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "When multimodality is implemented, do you think it is worth supporting multimodal \u2192 language-only conversions? Like InternVL3 38B is 6B of ViT, so some significant memory can be saved, if vision isn't needed. Alternatively, those layers can be disabled during inference, but then you'd still download and store them.\r\n\r\nOr just do such conversions externally to exllamav3?\r\n\r\nIf implemented here, it can be something like\r\n\r\n```py\r\n{\r\n  \"Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration\": (\"MistralForCausalLM\", \"language_model.\"),\r\n  \"InternVLForConditionalGeneration\": (\"Qwen2ForCausalLM\", \"language_model.\"),\r\n  # ...\r\n}\r\n\r\n# use this map when convert.py is asked for a language-only conversion\r\n# allow safetensors to load layers with a prefix\r\n# everything will see prefixless layer names and save them as such\r\n# then convert config.json\r\n```",
      "content_sha256": "08acd84bba8f8cec9c25a19e62dbc5b87d8f8f98f17ff98c5ae26ad605a5300a",
      "created_at": "2025-05-05T03:14:18Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-05T03:33:11Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6p3I5U",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/25#issuecomment-2849803860"
    }
  ]
}

    {
      "author_login": "DekoMoon",
      "content": "### Summary

git clone https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3.git

- Next, `convert.py`
```

- LLM Model: shisa-ai/shisa-v2-unphi4-14b (base model is unsloth/phi-4)
  - Link: https://huggingface.co/shisa-ai/shisa-v2-unphi4-14b



### CLI Output
```

```",

```python
        if params["capture"][self.qmap]["first_key"] == self.key:
            rows = np.prod(x.shape[:-1])
            dim = x.shape[-1]

            print(f'Shape: {x.shape}')

It was a bit long so I copied the output to here: https://pastebin.com/ntmUytvK",

      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/16#issuecomment-2808619050"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "DekoMoon",
      "content": "Interesting, it seems like unsloth/phi-4 with the same architecture, `LlamaForCausalLM`, was able to run layer 0 fine. I'll leave it running over night and see what happens.",
      "content_sha256": "08d0da973ba0a1560c59dd483503c9e7a3f7a60c3327b1fdc57058e22b6d2760",
      "created_at": "2025-04-16T08:05:19Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-16T08:05:19Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6nagsT",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/16#issuecomment-2808744723"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "DekoMoon",
      "content": "Quantizing `unsloth/phi-4` seemed to have [worked](https://huggingface.co/owentruong/phi-4-EXL3).

I am not sure why, but for some reason, the finetune version, `shisa-ai/shisa-v2-unphi4-14b`, doesn't work. Tried running another finetune version, `LightningRodLabs/Flashlight-v1.0`, and it seem to be able to run layer 0.

(note that `shisa-ai/shisa-v2-unphi4-14b` worked with exl2)",
      "content_sha256": "406e1c5a210b2abc36121f84d4c00f0958aca1393efa4d377f4fe66a3f1a4e32",
      "created_at": "2025-04-16T15:53:17Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-16T15:53:55Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6nfXeM",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/16#issuecomment-2810017676"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "The problem seems to be the tokenizer for the finetuned model. If you look in `tokenizer.json`, at the top of the file someone has added this:

```json
  "truncation": {
    "direction": "Right",
    "max_length": 4096,
    "strategy": "LongestFirst",
    "stride": 0
  },
```

I'm not sure what the purpose of that is, as it prevents the `tokenizers` library from tokenizing more than 4096 tokens, and the EXL3 quantizer needs much more than that. I suspect it's unintentionally left over from the finetuning process. But I'll make a note to check for it since apparently it's a thing that can happen, and the quantizer should notice rather than giving a cryptic CUDA error down the line.

In the meantime, quantization should work if you replace it with:

```json
  "truncation": null,
```

Or alternatively just copy `tokenizer.json` over from Phi-4, since they seem to be identical otherwise.",
      "content_sha256": "baedad3907e84db98c2c77dda624a5ebdac6af5c7a5cd6dce676f28ccd470a33",
      "created_at": "2025-04-17T18:23:30Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-17T18:23:30Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6ntgP3",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/16#issuecomment-2813723639"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "Okay, turns out you can just override that feature when loading the tokenizer. Problem solved.",
      "content_sha256": "727fd0a389392567451f6d7413b272d5875570f130853ca0a0af1067a5a38c07",
      "created_at": "2025-04-17T19:58:31Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-17T19:58:31Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6nuJLS",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/16#issuecomment-2813891282"
    }
  ]
}

items.title: humaneval.py: fix top_k type, remove rep_p, add qwen3
items.content:
{
  "discussion": {
    "author_login": "gakada",
    "created_at": "2025-05-11T03:34:41Z",
    "kind": "pull_request",
    "number": 35,
    "state": "CLOSED",
    "title": "humaneval.py: fix top_k type, remove rep_p, add qwen3",
    "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35"
  },
  "objects": [
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "Missed `top_k` being `int`, so it doesn't work as an index like that.",
      "content_sha256": "35fe80de09b855a2a38f1735318eb9e8f39c84ecd0db98b82bbc33e1146d78f9",
      "created_at": "2025-05-11T03:34:41Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-11T03:34:41Z",
      "source_id": "PR_kwDOOU24Gs6VuDLB",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "For `rep_p`, all of those break the generation here, so it gets 0%.\r\n\r\n```py\r\nrep_p = 1.01,\r\nrep_p = 1.01, rep_sustain_range = 10,\r\nrep_p = 1.01, rep_sustain_range = 10, rep_decay_range = 10,\r\nrep_p = 1.001, rep_sustain_range = 512, rep_decay_range = 512,\r\n```",
      "content_sha256": "2682d737aba56238259998611dc2abdecfc8ef6cec32af33c8bf89183ebc03a6",
      "created_at": "2025-05-11T05:32:04Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-11T06:13:49Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6rCQfG",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35#issuecomment-2869495750"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "`chatml` vs `qwen3` is ~30% vs ~50% on Qwen3-8B 4bpw and ~35% vs ~40% on 8bpw-h8 (and still many strange repetitive completions).",
      "content_sha256": "4071eaf7702d008dd43e2e8dc67127bf2b55bb81539f92799e6d3fcadf6017f1",
      "created_at": "2025-05-11T09:24:51Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-11T09:24:51Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6rC2f8",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35#issuecomment-2869651452"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "Qwen3-8B is very weird about its reasoning. The larger model appear to be more conditioned to reason and will often fall into reasoning patterns even outside of the `<think>` `</think>` tags. That's what those repetitive failures always look like, e.g.:\r\n\r\n```py\r\n    # Parse the fractions\r\n    x_num, x_den = x.split('/')\r\n    n_num, n_den = n.split('/')\r\n\r\n    # Multiply the fractions\r\n    # (x_num / x_den) * (n_num / n_den) = (x_num * n_num) / (x_den * n_den)\r\n    # Check if the result is a whole number\r\n    # To do this, we can check if the numerator is divisible by the denominator\r\n    # (x_num * n_num) % (x_den * n_den) == 0\r\n\r\n    # But since we are working with integers, we can also check if the result is a whole number\r\n    # by checking if the numerator is divisible by the denominator\r\n    # (x_num * n_num) % (x_den * n_den) == 0\r\n```\r\n\r\nThis is the type of stuff the model usually generates in its reasoning step, and it seems to work a lot better there, without needing repetition penalties to avoid falling into cycles. It seems like the non-reasoning mode is just sort of half-baked. The smaller Qwen3 models do a lot better with this style of prompting, to support that hypothesis. Qwen3-4B gets 78%, for instance. I think to actually get decent scores from Qwen3 in general the pipeline would have to allow for reasoning at the start of the prompt (i.e. generate until `</think>`, then inject the head of the function after that.\r\n\r\nRepetition penalties in general are a hack, and you can't rely on them to fix a model that's already in some failure mode. In this case I think it's a bug in the implementation, though. Something about the combination of the forced prefix and the penalties being enabled causes it to always sample `!!!!!!!` before doing anything else, e.g.:\r\n\r\n```py\r\ndef remove_vowels(text):\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    remove_vowels is a function that takes string and returns string without vowels.\r\n    >>> remove_vowels('')\r\n    ''\r\n    >>> remove_vowels(\"abcdef\\nghijklm\")\r\n    'bcdf\\nghjklm'\r\n    >>> remove_vowels('abcdef')\r\n    'bcdf'\r\n    >>> remove_vowels('aaaaa')\r\n    ''\r\n    >>> remove_vowels('aaBAA')\r\n    'B'\r\n    >>> remove_vowels('zbcd')\r\n    'zbcd'\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    !!!!!!!\r\n    vowels = \"aeiou\"\r\n    result = \"\"\r\n    for char in text:\r\n        if char not in vowels:\r\n            result += char\r\n    return result\r\n```\r\n\r\nI will investigate this in a little bit. As for the PR, it's fine and I'll merge once the dev branch is pushed in a little bit. Have you tried adding `/no_think` to the prompt and/or system prompt?",
      "content_sha256": "e5120ff7c17334c3dcbcba71f067a390cd36f0b2133dfa0598b50ff4d34f8a15",
      "created_at": "2025-05-11T15:11:23Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-11T15:11:23Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6rD7D4",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35#issuecomment-2869932280"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "Yep, I checked, and there was a bug in the penalty kernel. Masking out a token and then applying any penalty to it before the falloff range would result in `lerp(-inf, -inf, 1)`, which should yield `-inf` but is evalutated as `(-inf) * 1.0f + (-inf) * 0.0f = NaN`. In this case it was `<|im_end|>` being prohibited because of the `min_new_tokens` argument. Fix will appear in dev branch shortly.",
      "content_sha256": "a7a558367ce44b5f50bbd5187097c2242ec9895dd551b9266c82340b1f5dfeb5",
      "created_at": "2025-05-11T15:33:57Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-05-11T15:33:57Z",
      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6rD9X2",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/pull/35#issuecomment-2869941750"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "gakada",
      "content": "I didn't see any difference with `/no_think`, trying to generate functions bodies like that, with or without `/no_think`, can produce many placeholders (like `# Insert implementation here`) and bad repetitions (just repeating the same lines). `enable_thinking=False` seems better, i.e. starting the reply with `<think>\\n\\n</think>\\n\\n`, then it is only bad repetitions (less for Qwen3-14B). So yeah, probably just the non-thinking mode not working very well, like reka-flash-3 still manages to think in comments and isn't doing any placeholders or repetitions when trying to generate code before thinking blocks (but it will keep rambling in comments instead, Phi-4-R+ is also similar, also around 90%).
